outlookMethod: Win % for every remaining regular-season game = normal CDF((power gap + 2.5 home field) / 14.8), the same math as the main tracker. Projected record = current record + the sum of remaining win chances.

market: Timing is where a model earns its keep: when the Data Rating disagreed with the OPENING line by 4+ points, the line moved toward the model 66% of the time in 2025 (74% in 2024), but against the CLOSING line the model's side won only 51%. Lines absorb what the model knows by kickoff, so beating the close (CLV) is the honest scorecard.
Home teams beat the closing spread by about 0.85 points per game in both 2024 and 2025: a hint the market slightly underrates home field. Suggestive, not proven (about 2 standard errors).
Mixing 20–30% model with 70–80% closing line lowered the 2025 miss slightly (11.83 → 11.80): the model holds a little information the close doesn't.
backtest.totals: Totals: a pace × efficiency scoring environment did not beat the closing over/under. One pattern repeated in both years: when both offenses rate as efficient, games went slightly UNDER the total (corr −0.10 in 2024, −0.06 in 2025). Overs hit 51% in 2024 and 49% in 2025.
backtest.verdict: What predicts college football: a good preseason prior, this season's results with turnover luck partly removed, and success rate. Player matchups, travel and rest add nothing measurable once the line is known. The Player Model now uses that Data Rating in place of v1's EPA-only unit power.
sources: Action Network & Football Study Hall (turnover luck, wind, byes)
backtest.live2026: Live check on 2026 weeks 2–5 (220 games the model never saw): Data Rating 12.58, in-season results only 14.33, closing line 11.00. Same ordering as the backtest.
backtest.caveat: Honest caveat: the final settings (prior worth 2 games, half-strength luck, which inputs to drop) were chosen after seeing 2025 results, so 12.14 is slightly optimistic (by about 0.05 points). The 2026 check is clean.

method:
Player-impact model ("PM") for the current week.

Player Model v2 (Oct 9, 2026, after the research backtest in model/research*.py):
PM Power = 0.6 x Claude Power + 0.4 x Data Rating + QB adjustment + injury adjustments.
 - Data Rating (model/data_rating.py): last season's final SP+ and roster talent as a prior worth 2 games, fading as games are
   played, plus this season's results (turnover luck half-removed) and opponent-adjusted success rate (garbage time removed).
   Centred on Claude Power's FBS mean. Backtest (fit 2024, test 2025, weeks 2+): 12.14 pts average miss vs 13.32 for in-season
   results alone and 11.83 for the closing line. v1 used opponent-adjusted EPA/play alone (no prior), which was weakest early.
 - QB adjustment: only when the starter changes; 0.5 x (current starter's pass EPA/dropback - team season QB EPA/dropback) x dropbacks/game.
   Halved on purpose: in QB-change games the closing line over-reacted to the new QB's form in 2024 and 2025.
 - Injury adjustments (input injuries.json): starting QB out -> backup (or replacement level) instead; skill player out -> -0.5 x his
   EPA added per game (cap 3); top havoc defender out -> up to -1.5 by his share of team TFL+sacks. Rough by design.
 - Matchup interactions (run game vs defensive front, protection vs pass rush, ...) are shown as notes with ZERO weight:
   none predicted margins or totals out of sample (see model/out/*.txt).
Usage: python model/player_model.py <year> <week> [injuries.json]  -> model/out/playermodel_<year>_w<week>.json
